correctness.rationale: Backward Poisson renewal gives a stationary Beta(1,alpha) GEM expansion with unit-sphere vectors. Conditional pair inner products are centered, pairwise uncorrelated and have variance exactly 1/d. Explicit beta stick recursions give E H, E H^2 and E K, hence the exact finite-d L2 and variance formulae. A common normalized Gaussian-coordinate coupling proves almost-sure convergence. For each finite set of pairs a multivariate Gaussian-array CLT gives independent standard normal inner-product limits, while the omitted infinite pairs have conditional fluctuation variance bounded by four times H times the squared-weight tail, which tends to zero. Conditional characteristic functions and the delta method then prove both limiting distributions. Actual package code checks finite rational identities and finite Monte Carlo comparisons; none substitutes for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The high-dimensional radial behavior is a motivated unaddressed regime of a fully specified active-particle stationary law. It exhibits persistent sample-to-sample renewal-history uncertainty despite angular isotropization, and the first correction is a history-dependent Gaussian mixture rather than a single Gaussian. The exact finite-d coupling error makes the limiting law quantitatively testable, while the conditional fluctuation theorem provides a new benchmark beyond tabulated moments and low-dimensional densities.
